Formulation
- Predisposing: Family history of migraine, exposure to serious illness in friend’s family, individual tendency to worry under stress
- Precipitating: Recent stressful events at work; similar recent headache episode; recent bereavement/stressor (friend’s mother’s death from brain tumor)
- Perpetuating: Ongoing workplace stress, lack of effective coping strategies, health anxiety exacerbated by internet searches and recent experiences
- Protective: Willingness to seek help, insight into worries, open to management strategies

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Health anxiety relating to fears of serious illness (brain tumor)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduce anxiety and fear about health
  - Achieve reassurance regarding headaches
  - Regain confidence to return to work
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Support patient to manage health-related anxiety
  - Provide education and tools for symptom monitoring and management
  - Monitor for escalation or persistence of health anxiety
- Actions (Patient):
  - Refrain from excessive online symptom-checking
  - Maintain a headache diary
  - Return for urgent review if concerning symptoms develop (worsening headache, new neurological symptoms)
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide explanation and education about migraines and health anxiety
  - Reinforce safety-netting and criteria for urgent review
  - Offer review appointment to discuss progress and management options, including possible prophylactic medication for migraine

Secondary Problem: Migraine-type headache
- Patient Goal(s): Achieve symptom relief and minimize impact on daily functioning/work
- Clinical Goal(s): Effective acute symptom management, consider prophylactic medication if headaches recur
- Actions (Patient):
  - Use recommended pain relief as discussed
  - Record headache patterns and possible triggers
  - Rest and self-care as needed
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Advise on acute medications and self-care measures
  - Plan for follow-up/review of headache diary and response to treatment

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Migraine features, health anxiety, headache diary, warning signs for urgent review, appropriate use of medications
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Worsening headache, neurological deficits, persistent visual changes, increased anxiety or inability to cope, further work absence due to symptoms
- Coping Strategies: Symptom monitoring, stress identification, safe reassurance-seeking, limiting unhelpful internet searches
